                    ### Question
                    A 43-year-old man consulted for diarrheal syndrome, and reported among his background 3 pneumonias in adulthood. Which of the following immunological studies should we request ?:

                    ### Options
                    opa. Serum immunoglobulin count and antibody production capacity test.
opb. Phagocytosis test and oxidative metabolism of neutrophils.
opc. Apoptosis test (programmed cell death) in the circulating lymphocytes of the patient.
opd. Study of the repertoire and clonality of the T lymphocytes (alpha / beta).
ope. In this patient, it would not be appropriate to request any immunological study.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Given the patient's history of recurrent infections and diarrheal syndrome, it is appropriate to request both serum immunoglobulin count and antibody production capacity test as well as the study of the repertoire and clonality of the T lymphocytes (alpha/beta). These tests can help evaluate potential immune system impairment and underlying immunodeficiency. Phagocytosis test and oxidative metabolism of neutrophils may also be considered due to the clinical presentation suggestive of immune dysfunction.
